Increasing diversity in clinical trials will help us increase diversity in Alzheimer’s research, treatment, and prevention.

Let's find a cure once and for all – together. (4/4)

Delaware has the nation’s 5th highest rate of pregnant women with substance use disorder. 

Thanks to a federal grant, Gaudenzia's in-patient substance use treatment facility — that will open this summer — will help get pregnant women the treatment and care they need.

Today, I'll be voting YES on the #RestoringHope for Mental Health and Well-Being Act to strengthen more than 30 programs that support mental health care and substance use disorder prevention, care, treatment, and recovery support.

That’s why today I sent a letter to the Biden Administration with 48 of my House colleagues to ask the Center for Medicare & Medicaid to clarify patient care rights as they relate to pregnancy and abortion care under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Active Labor Act. (2/2) https://t.co/0tmKBBjhs1

This is a huge deal.

The Break the Cycle of Violence Act invests in the kind of wraparound services that can not only help address the symptoms of violence we see in our communities but also address the root causes of that violence.

We can & will break the cycle of violence.

This morning, after experiencing mild symptoms, I tested positive for COVID. I’m feeling okay and am grateful to be vaccinated and double-boosted. I will be isolating and following CDC guidance.

I encourage all Delawareans to get vaccinated if they haven't already. And #GoBirds!

It's important to me that we increase awareness of the signs and symptoms of pulmonary embolisms so that we can save lives.

Thank you to advocates @khoff09, her mom, and Leslie from @StopTheClot for sharing their stories with me. I'm proud to stand with you in this fight! https://t.co/DPWjTwIcQS

The Ronald McDonald House Charities of Greater Delaware provides a home-away-from-home for kids going through treatment and their families.

Thanks to the RMHC of Greater Delaware staff for giving me a tour of “the House” yesterday where I saw its services and support first hand. https://t.co/piTGWOvouh

This week marks 9 years since losing the love of my life, Charles, to blood clots.

Today, I introduced the bipartisan Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention and Treatment Act to raise awareness of the signs and symptoms of blood clots and pulmonary embolisms. (1/2) https://t.co/9KFDtfTo0B

The Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention and Treatment Act isn’t just about honoring my late husband, Charles, who died from blood clots - it’s also about saving lives.

Awareness of the signs and symptoms, like who is most at risk, can help us do just that.

📽️: @coasttvnews https://t.co/24NhkSMimG

.@CDCgov provides information on the signs and symptoms of blood clots and pulmonary embolisms. Click below to learn more.👇🏽

https://t.co/Ivm3Lh0kSS

Kate Cox's experience of trying to exercise her reproductive freedom in Texas - forcing her to travel out of state for abortion care - is a harrowing example of what women have been experiencing since Roe v. Wade was overturned.

Congress must act to protect reproductive freedom.

On Maternal Health Awareness Day, I recommit myself to supporting the health and wellness of moms everywhere.

Moms in the U.S. are dying at the highest rate in the developed world. It’s unacceptable - and it's up to Congress to support evidence-based solutions to fix it. 🧵

On National Black HIV & AIDS Awareness Day, let's remember those we’ve lost & commit to expanding access to HIV testing, prevention, and treatment.

We’ve made a lot of progress in ending the stigma surrounding HIV, but we must do more, especially for the Black community. #NBHAAD

Last year, I introduced the Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention & Treatment Act in honor of my late husband who died from blood clots.

I was humbled and honored to receive the 2024 Blood Clot Awareness Champion Award from the National Blood Clot Association. https://t.co/Pg7pLyOCDp

As #NationalBloodClotAwarenessMonth ends, I'm proud to highlight my bipartisan Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention and Treatment Act, named in honor of my late husband who died from blood clots.

We all must learn the signs and symptoms of blood clots so we can #StopTheClot. https://t.co/3bMCop4Uo7

Excited to be in Middletown today with Mayor Ken Branner and Dr. Kevin Spence of the Delaware League of Local Governments!

We saw how American Rescue Plan Act funding is helping Middletown increase its wastewater treatment capacity to keep up with the Town's rapid growth. https://t.co/idHU6M2NoS

Thank you to the Wilmington Alumnae Chapter of @dstinc1913 for hosting their Empowering our Sisters: Our Journey to Wellness summit in Newark. I was proud to discuss the importance of awareness, action, & advocacy when it comes to blood clots - and how they can affect any of us. https://t.co/pfr75iS0wj

One year ago today, I introduced the Charles Rochester Blood Clot Prevention and Treatment Act – bipartisan legislation honoring my late husband who died from blood clots.

As a member of @EnergyCommerce, this issue is professional. But as Lisa, it's personal. #StopTheClot https://t.co/h3n1Lnny2K

Federal workers who show up every day looking for ways to improve the lives of people all across the country deserve better than the treatment they’ve received from this administration.

Playing games with the lives of hard working public servants isn’t efficiency, it’s cruelty.

The AIDS crisis - which claimed the lives of hundreds of thousands of Americans - was made much worse by leaders who stood in the way of life-saving research & treatment.

I urge this administration to reconsider and reinvest in global prevention. Countless lives are on the line.

Freezing funding for Planned Parenthood would hurt countless patients and millions of people who won’t be able to get the health care they need – birth control, cancer screenings, STI testing and treatment, or even wellness exams.

The cruelty agenda continues.

This assumption that people on Medicaid don’t want to work is just wrong.

For folks like my constituent Emmanuel, Medicaid is the lifeline they need to get and hold a job.

The best health care is health care.

For countless Delawareans and folks across the country, Medicaid plays a vital role in everyday life.

This month, I called Emmanuel - who is able to work and pay rent thanks to Medicaid - and Nancy - whose son relies on Medicaid for long-term care - to hear their stories. https://t.co/lAanaak75L

Constituents have told me how Medicaid empowers them to hold jobs, live normal lives, and participate as full members of society. 

They’re not going to just “get over it.”

When we hear from people back home about policies we’re voting on, our job is to listen.
